items.text: fixed: the heads-up display's footer band now runs edge to edge and down to the pop-up's lower edge: its tab buttons fill the band's full height, with no wasted strip beneath. The yellow mark above the open tab is a straight line sitting right on the border between the band and the pane above, with no rounded ends, as in the side menus.

added: a Settings section in the Index, as in Current. Words: Always, Learn (the default: a control's word shows at first, then fades once you have used it about five times, and comes back when you press it) or Never (icons only; screen readers still hear every word). Theme: Auto, Light or Dark. Both are kept on this device.

changed: a scene is now a score, everywhere you read it: the bar's previous and next score, the dice ("roll a new score"), the status line ("Score 1 of 1"), the Scores tab and pane, the index and the guide. A score is the musical state: the grid, the lines, the tempo and the feel. "Scene" is kept for a future visual layer. The export that was called "score" is now called "notation" so the word means one thing.
changed: "Past scenes" is now just "Scenes" (the heads-up display's tab and pane, the index, the guide): they are scenes, and nothing in Battanboo is a future scene.

changed: the Past scenes tab and its pane title in the heads-up display wear their own icon, four softly rounded squares (many scenes at once). The tab had borrowed the bar's back arrow, which looks like the display's own previous-pane arrow, and the title showed the display icon.

changed: holding the robot opens the line-ups as a tall pop-up directly above the robot button, on a phone and on a computer alike (it used to sit at the far right edge, or open the heads-up display). It has no close button: tap anywhere else, or choose a line-up, and it goes away. Slide a finger up or down the list to try them.
added: an Install section in the Index, as in Current: it works out your device and browser and shows how to keep Battanboo as its own app, with a link to send someone straight to it.

added: Automation has a third field switch, Follow with a melody (off). A quiet line in the field follows the notes that are playing: every couple of beats it steps to a scale neighbour or leaps to a note it just heard, and sometimes rests. It stops with the robot.
